headline: Majors hold above the 200-day line while funding costs spike across alts; whale repositioning shifts from selling into exchanges to buying and storing off-chain
paragraphs: The regime is mixed but sturdy. Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana, XRP, and BNB all trade above their 200-day simple moving averages, a six-of-seven picture that grounds the setup. Only ADA sits below, a laggard down 76.5 percent from its 12-month peak. The crosses tell a different story. Bitcoin and XRP show no golden cross, signaling that the 50-day remains below the 200-day despite current price sitting above it; Ethereum, Solana, and BNB have crossed, suggesting a faster climb already underway. MACD diverges sharply: only BNB and ADA print above their signal lines, while Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana, XRP, and Doge all print below. Momentum is cooling even as prices hold the longer trend, a common rest pattern in uptrends rather than a reversal flag at this stage.

Positioning reveals two layers. On the major contracts, funding is nearly flat. Bitcoin's 8-hour rate sits at 0.05 basis points annualized to 0.5 percent, Ethereum at 1.8 percent, both moderate and not crowding long positions into unsustainable cost. But zoom to the smaller caps and funding spikes into warning territory. Solana trades at 3.7 percent annualized, XRP at 7.8 percent, and Doge at 2.5 percent, while long-to-short ratios balloon to 1.97, 2.48, and 3.45 respectively, meaning longs are outnumbering shorts by nearly two or three to one. This is classic positioning risk in the alts: the money to hold long leverage is expensive and concentrated. Over the last 7 to 16 hours, liquidations have favored shorts across the board (Solana 319,783 dollars of shorts liquidated versus 72,892 of longs, XRP 491,595 versus 267,955), the signature of price rallies flushing bearish bets. Bitcoin and Ethereum show the reverse, shorts getting cleaned more aggressively, a sign the majors are grinding higher without shocking moves.

Flows paint a regime shift in progress. Over the past three weeks, whales were net sellers into exchanges: week ending August 15 saw 508 million dollars of Bitcoin flow onto exchanges, August 22 saw 1,062 million dollars, and August 29 saw 659 million dollars. In the week ending September 5, the direction flipped. Whales moved 494 million dollars of Bitcoin off exchanges, with three large tranches out of Coinbase Institutional (51.5 million dollars each) in the last 24 hours. That off-exchange buying is the behavior of hodlers rotating into cold storage or private custody, a tightening of the float. Spot ETF flows affirm the institutional bid: Bitcoin saw 174.6 million dollars of inflow on September 4 and 986.7 million dollars over the last five sessions, with three of five days in the same direction. Ethereum's flows are lighter at 25.9 million dollars on the day and 215.3 million dollars on the five-session net, but positive and intact. Stablecoin float stands at 310.5 billion dollars, up 1.48 percent over the month, ample dry powder sitting on the sidelines.

Sentiment reads Greed at 73, the upper end of the 30-day range (27 to 74), yet the tape shows measured accumulation rather than euphoric buying. Fear and Greed gauges crowd psychology; the money does different work. Spot inflows persist, whales are storing rather than dumping, and major asset classes hold structural uptrends. The tension is in the alts: high funding, lopsided longs, and violent one-day moves (BNB up 6.28 percent, Doge up 6.02 percent, ARB up 34.62 percent) suggest momentum traders, not conviction holders. Price on the day is mixed; Ethereum is up 1.0 percent and XRP up 1.0 percent, but ETH down 0.99 percent on the week and XRP down 0.65 percent on the week, a common pattern when short-term bounces fight structural softness.

The central watch is whether funding in the alts corrects before the longs get flushed. Bitcoin sits 36 percent below its 12-month high, Ethereum 47 percent below, Solana 58 percent below; all are far from panic lows but far from peaks. If XRP funding (7.8 percent annualized) stays elevated and the 2.48 long-to-short ratio persists, the next down move will be sharp and fast. On the flip side, if whales continue to buy dips and move coins off exchanges while spot ETF flows stay positive, the correction becomes a buying opportunity rather than a cascade. Bitcoin network difficulty is rising 2.5 percent at the next retarget (1,993 blocks remain), a sign of stable mining interest and a subtle bullish tail wind. The key condition to monitor: when does BNB's MACD, the sole major with momentum above signal, roll over to join the rest, or does the rest catch up?
